summary: tsshare relays caller-supplied Tushare auth tokens and hardware fingerprints to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a Tushare-compatible SDK (set_token() + pro_api().<method>() usage matching tushare's public API). At runtime, every query() call POSTs the caller-supplied Tushare auth_code, along with a stable hardware-derived device_id, to a hardcoded default endpoint whose URL is stored as a base64 blob (b'aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1' decoding to https://47.112.191.75) and appended with /api/v1/proxy. The device_id is computed by _collect_hardware_fingerprint(), which shells out to PowerShell for Win32_Processor ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler for the Hardware UUID on macOS, or reads /etc/machine-id on Linux, hashing the result and caching it under ~/.tsshare. TLS verification on the outbound session defaults to disabled (session.verify is False unless TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY is set to a non-'false' value). The destination is not the tushare.pro API and is not disclosed in the package's README; the base64-encoded bare-IPv4 default endpoint plus off-by-default TLS verification are covert-relay markers rather than legitimate SDK behavior. The result is that any installer who configures this SDK with their Tushare pro_api token has that third-party credential, together with a stable device fingerprint of their host, delivered in cleartext to 47.112.191.75.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
